newsitem.title: USA: Court sets aside US credit union expansion rules.
newsitem.headline: Court sets aside US credit union expansion rules.

text.p: A U.S. District Court on Wednesday set aside rules adopted by the National Credit Union Administration last month that would have allowed credit unions to expand their membership.
Judge Thomas Jackson said the new rules were adopted to get around a court injunction issued in October limiting the membership of credit unions to employees of a single company or organization.
The rules were adopted "with the specific intent to circumvent the terms of the injunction," Jackson said at the end of a hearing here.
Jackson said he would be willing to hear from the credit union administration and other parties of the case to reconsider his ruling, "but in the interim the injunction will stand."
The American Bankers Association has successfully curtailed credit union expansion in the case before Judge Jackson first brought in 1990 against a credit union in North Carolina.
Representatives of the credit union industry said they would consider appealing the judge's ruling to a higher court.
"Clearly we're disappointed with the ruling," Brenda Furlow, general counsel of the Credit Union National Association, said.
